Hi Kimberly,

Nice to e-meet you — I'm Alex, Head of Integrations at SecureAudit LLC. We run a GRC platform used by several SaaS vendors to ingest SOC2 artifacts and pen-test reports directly from vendor evidence endpoints. One of our larger customers is asking for an automated feed from Redwood so they can pull artifacts for continuous monitoring.

High-level asks from our side:
- Standard API or SFTP ingestion endpoint for signed artifacts (we prefer API)
- Signed S3 presigned URLs or time-limited download links for large report artifacts
- Proof of tamper-evidence metadata (SHA256 or similar) attached to each artifact
- A short onboarding SLA and an initial cadence for delivery (weekly vs on-demand)

Could you point me at the right person to scope a connector and an SOW? Happy to share a short mutual action plan template. I can include procurement and security in follow-ups.

Thanks,

Hi all — quick technical note from the infra side.

We have two viable integration patterns:
1) Push API: Redwood exposes a /v1/evidence/push endpoint with JWT bearer auth; payload includes manifest metadata (sha256, size, timestamp) and either the binary (multipart) or a presigned download link. Works well for on-demand flows and real-time pushes.
2) Pull API: SecureAudit can poll a /v1/evidence/list endpoint and then GET presigned URLs for artifacts. Better for periodic batch pulls.

For tamper evidence we sign the manifest with our service key and include a signer_id header. mTLS is available but requires additional cert provisioning (we can do a short cert-exchange window during onboarding).

I’ve attached a connector spec draft with example payloads and auth headers.

Marcus Lin
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
